insights.topic: Verified purchase signal vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: The protocol settles attribution at ~$0.10 per verified receipt versus $5–$150 CPA for probabilistic ad tech — a 50–200x cost delta that isn't a marginal efficiency gain, it's a structural difference between inference and cryptographic proof of purchase.

With Chrome completing cookie deprecation and device fingerprinting increasingly blocked by privacy regulation, the ad industry has lost its primary cross-site tracking primitives — and first-party data only covers what happens inside one company's walls.

Amazon knows Amazon purchases; Walmart knows Walmart purchases; neither knows the other — and no existing solution produces identity-free, cross-ecosystem purchase signals that any third party can query.

insights.topic: Geographic diffusion as organic demand signal
insights.insight: Simultaneous activation across non-contiguous metros — non-metro Hawaii, Arizona, South Carolina, and North Carolina entering in the same burst cycles — indicates word-of-mouth propagation through social graph topology, not paid acquisition, which means adoption is self-sustaining rather than spend-dependent.

The 7-day velocity reading hit 0.888x on March 22 — the highest in recent cycles and a decisive break above the sub-0.75x floor that had persisted for weeks — with a 47-receipt expansion in a single 27-minute window representing the sharpest intraday burst in the current dataset.

Existing receipt platforms like Fetch and Ibotta hold real purchase data but it is identity-attached, closed-loop, and not queryable by third parties — the structural gap is a privacy-safe, cryptographically verified signal that crosses ecosystem boundaries without creating regulatory liability.
